LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Listening for gist

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for gist. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you greet others?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basic greetings for learning
2. greet others using acquired structures
3. appreciate the role of greetings in society
4. identify general information from listening texts
5. imitate given structures for communication
6. appreciate the role imitation plays in language acquisition
7. recognise words related to home for learning
8. speak words imitatively related to home for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR GIST
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for gist helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR GIST
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify basic greetings for learning

What this means
In this part you learn to identify basic greetings for learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify basic greetings for learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify basic greetings for learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Greet others using acquired structures

What this means
In this part you learn to greet others using acquired structures. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: greet others using acquired structures.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for gist to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can greet others using acquired structures. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of greetings in society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of greetings in society. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of greetings in society.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of greetings in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify general information from listening texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify general information from listening texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify general information from listening texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify general information from listening texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Imitate given structures for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to imitate given structures for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: imitate given structures for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for gist to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can imitate given structures for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Appreciate the role imitation plays in language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role imitation plays in language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role imitation plays in language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role imitation plays in language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for gist is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify basic greetings for learning)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for gist to a partner. (skill: greet others using acquired structures)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of greetings in society)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify general information from listening texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for gist to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify basic greetings for learning.
3. Practise this skill: greet others using acquired structures.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of greetings in society.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for gist from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for gist: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Listening for gist?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you greet others?
2. How do we get the main idea from a listening text?
3. Why do we imitate?
4. Why is proper articulation important when speaking?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for gist means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify basic greetings for learning.
5. Be able to: greet others using acquired structures.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
